name: Quadrantids
note: a sharp peak only a few hours wide, so the date matters more than usual

name: Lyrids
note: modest rates, but it throws the occasional bright fireball

name: Eta Aquariids
note: dust from Halley's comet; much better from the southern hemisphere

name: Southern Delta Aquariids
note: a broad peak spread over several nights, so any of them will do

name: Perseids
note: the reliable one, and warm nights to watch it in

name: Draconids
note: usually quiet but has produced storms; best in the evening, not after midnight

name: Orionids
note: Halley's dust again, from the other side of its orbit

name: Southern Taurids
note: slow and bright, worth it despite the low rate

name: Northern Taurids
note: slow and bright, worth it despite the low rate

name: Leonids
note: storms roughly every 33 years; ordinary in between

name: Geminids
note: the richest shower of the year, and it starts early in the evening

name: Ursids
note: circumpolar from mid-northern latitudes, so it runs all night
